name: Warlock
summary: Across Azeroth, Warlocks wield forbidden powers that bring fear and distrust. They command demons and cast curses, fire, and shadow magic. Some turn these arts against the Burning Legion and its servants.

sections.title: Forbidden Arts
sections.body:
Where ordinary spellcasters see ruin, warlocks see a path to victory. They strike from afar with shadow and fire, and drain the vital essence and souls of their enemies to fuel their fiercest rites. Brimstone falls from the sky, and agonizing curses break the mind.

Warlocks wear simple cloth and have little strength to withstand a blow. They call horrors to meet danger and sacrifice demonic thralls to preserve their own lives.

sections.title: Demonic Servitude
sections.body:
A warlock's hold over the Twisting Nether begins with small bargains and grows into iron dominion. Novices command mischievous imps to hurl flame. With deeper knowledge of fel magic, they bind voidwalkers from shadowy depths to bear physical punishment, succubi who beguile enemy minds, and ravenous felhunters that devour magical energy.

Each summon demands dangerous focus. The Nether's denizens are ever testing their masters for weakness.

sections.title: A Legacy of Ruin
sections.body:
Orcish demonology began on Draenor, where Kil'jaeden, a demon lord, tempted Gul'dan with the promise of supreme power. Gul'dan founded the secretive Shadow Council and turned many shaman into masters of fel magic. Demonic magic withered Draenor's fertile plains into a barren red wasteland, and the Old Horde invaded through the Dark Portal.

Among humans, the Kirin Tor forbade demonology and hunted illicit summonings. Yet ambitious mages still fell to the lure of untamed sorcery.

sections.title: Tolerated Pariahs
sections.body:
Warlocks now walk a narrow path between usefulness and execution. In Stormwind, they meet in hidden, gloomy tavern basements, away from the Cathedral of Light's watchful eyes. In Orgrimmar, they gather in the shadowed chasms of the Cleft of Shadow, watched by Thrall's shamanistic regime.

Their methods inspire revulsion, yet neither the Alliance nor the Horde can dismiss the edge warlock magic brings to a hostile battlefield.

faq.q: What makes a warlock different from a mage?
faq.answer: Mages use the ordered structure of arcane magic to shape fire, frost, and energy. Warlocks cross its safe bounds for chaotic fel magic, shadow, and demons. Many began as mages, then grew impatient with academic limits and sought forbidden shortcuts to power.

aliases: why does the alliance allow warlocks
faq.answer: Not every warlock is wicked, though warlock magic is dangerous and corruptive. Many fall into madness or join demonic cults. Others pledge loyalty to their faction and wield dark sorcery, stolen souls, and bound demons against threats such as the Scourge and the Burning Legion.

faq.q: How do warlocks summon and control demons?
faq.answer: Warlocks draw creatures from the Twisting Nether with ritual circles, dark incantations, and soul energy. They must break each demon's will and bind it through sheer mental dominance. If their focus slips, the demon may slaughter its master.

faq.q: Where did orc warlocks come from?
faq.answer: Orc warlocks began on Draenor, when Kil'jaeden turned Gul'dan from shamanism to demonic sorcery. Gul'dan formed the Shadow Council and trained other orcs. Fel corruption spread across their homeland until Draenor's soil withered and died.

faq.q: Why do the Alliance and Horde tolerate warlocks in their cities?
faq.answer: Neither faction trusts warlocks. In Stormwind and Ironforge, they practice in secret basements and forgotten tunnels to avoid public outrage. In Orgrimmar, they are kept in the Cleft of Shadow. Leaders tolerate them because their curses and summons are effective weapons in wartime.

faq.q: What are soul shards used for?
faq.answer: Warlocks drain the living essence of defeated enemies to make crystallized soul shards. These fragments hold the raw power to bypass natural magical laws, summon monstrous demons, and cast their most destructive spells.

Humans and gnomes practice as warlocks in the Alliance. In the Horde, orcs, trolls, and the Forsaken do. Dwarves, night elves, tauren, and the Skyborne do not. Wherever they live, warlocks are tolerated rather than trusted.

angles.text: As a mage, you may view warlocks with contempt and fear. Their dealings with the Nether seem undisciplined and put all mortal life at risk.
As a shaman, you remember how Gul'dan's fel sorcery severed your ancestors' ties to the spirits and killed Draenor's land. That is why shaman despise warlock magic above all else.
As an orc, you bear the bitter stain of the Old Horde's blood curse when you practice demonology. Some orcs keep these arts to survive in a hostile world.
As a paladin, you consider demonic summoning an abominable heresy. You watch warlocks who practice it with open hostility.
As a troll, you begin warlock training beside orc initiates in the Valley of Trials. Thrall's Horde watches every wielder of fel magic with the same wariness.
